subject: accounting
topic: Cash book (two- and three-column) and discounts

kept.q: What best describes a cash book in financial accounting?
options: A book of original entry that records both cash and bank transactions as they occur
A ledger account used only for recording fixed assets
A statement that shows the profit or loss for a trading period
A record that shows only credit sales and credit purchases
kept.explanation: The cash book is a book of original entry (and also serves as a ledger account) that records all cash and bank receipts and payments in the order they happen. It is not used for fixed assets, profit/loss, or credit transactions alone.
kept.pidgin: Cash book na book wey dem dey use record all cash and bank transactions as e dey happen. E no be for fixed assets, profit/loss, or only credit transactions.

kept.q: In a three-column cash book, what are the discount columns used for?
options: Recording trade discount allowed on bulk purchases of goods
Recording cash discount allowed to debtors and cash discount received from creditors
Recording only the discount received from suppliers each month
Recording bad debts written off at the end of the year
kept.explanation: The discount columns in a three-column cash book are memorandum columns that record cash discount allowed (to customers who pay promptly) and cash discount received (from suppliers when we pay promptly). Trade discount and bad debts are not recorded here.
kept.pidgin: Di discount columns for three-column cash book na to show discount wey we give customers (discount allowed) and discount wey suppliers give us (discount received) when payment dey done quick. Trade discount and bad debt no dey enter dia.

kept.q: Chidinma's cash column in her cash book showed an opening balance of ₦5,000. During the week she received ₦12,000 cash from a customer and paid ₦3,500 cash for stationery. What is the closing cash balance?
kept.explanation: Closing cash balance = Opening balance + Receipts - Payments = 5,000 + 12,000 - 3,500 = ₦13,500.
kept.pidgin: Closing cash balance = Opening balance + wetin enter - wetin comot = 5,000 + 12,000 - 3,500 = ₦13,500.

kept.q: A contra entry in a three-column cash book arises in which of the following situations?
options: When goods are sold on credit to a customer
When the discount allowed for the period exceeds the discount received
When a cheque received earlier from a customer is dishonoured by the bank
When cash is withdrawn from the bank for office use, affecting both the cash and bank columns
kept.explanation: A contra entry occurs when a transaction affects both the cash column and the bank column of the same cash book, such as withdrawing cash from the bank for office use (debit cash, credit bank). Credit sales, discount comparisons, and dishonoured cheques do not create contra entries by themselves.
kept.pidgin: Contra entry dey happen when one transaction touch both cash and bank columns for same cash book, like when person comot money from bank go use for office (debit cash, credit bank). Credit sales or dishonoured cheque no be contra entry by demsef.

kept.q: Mr. Okafor owed a supplier ₦40,000. He paid the full debt by cheque within the discount period and enjoyed a 5% cash discount for prompt payment. How much did he actually pay?
kept.explanation: Discount = 5% of ₦40,000 = ₦2,000. Amount paid = ₦40,000 - ₦2,000 = ₦38,000. The debt reduces because of the discount received for paying promptly.
kept.pidgin: Discount = 5% of ₦40,000 = ₦2,000. Wetin e pay = ₦40,000 - ₦2,000 = ₦38,000. Di debt reduce because e pay fast fast make im enjoy discount.

kept.q: A trader's three-column cash book showed opening bank balance of ₦25,000. During the month: (i) received a cheque of ₦18,000 from a debtor and banked it; (ii) paid rent by cheque, ₦6,000; (iii) withdrew ₦5,000 cash from the bank for office use (a contra entry); (iv) paid a supplier by cheque, ₦10,000. What is the closing bank balance?
kept.explanation: Closing bank balance = 25,000 + 18,000 (cheque received) - 6,000 (rent) - 5,000 (withdrawal to cash) - 10,000 (supplier) = ₦22,000. Discounts allowed or received do not affect the bank column figure directly.
kept.pidgin: Closing bank balance = 25,000 + 18,000 (cheque wey enter) - 6,000 (rent) - 5,000 (wey e comot go cash) - 10,000 (supplier) = ₦22,000. Discount no dey change the bank column amount directly.

kept.q: A trader bought goods on credit worth ₦60,000 from Alhaji Musa. He later returned defective goods worth ₦5,000. He paid the balance owed in cash within the discount period and enjoyed a 2% cash discount on the amount paid. How much discount did he receive?
kept.explanation: Balance owed after returns = 60,000 - 5,000 = ₦55,000. Discount received = 2% of 55,000 = ₦1,100. The discount is calculated on the net balance, not the original purchase amount.
kept.pidgin: Balance after return = 60,000 - 5,000 = ₦55,000. Discount wey e receive = 2% of 55,000 = ₦1,100. Na di balance wey remain dem use calculate discount, no be di original amount.

q.q: A two-column cash book normally has which pair of columns on each side?
options: Bank column and discount column only
Cash column and discount column only
q.explanation: A two-column cash book records both cash and bank transactions side by side, with a cash column and a bank column on each side (debit and credit). Discount columns are added to make it a three-column cash book.
q.pidgin: Two-column cash book get cash column and bank column for both sides (debit and credit). If dem add discount column, na so e become three-column cash book.
